title: Evolution without evolution: Dynamics described by stationary observables

title: Time and the interpretation of canonical quantum gravity
version: Phys. Rev. D 40, 2598-2614 (1989-10-15); DOI 10.1103/PhysRevD.40.2598 (Crossref verified; PubMed corroborates 40(8):2598-2614)
locators: Full text read via public PDF at pitp.phas.ubc.ca (PITP 7 Pines 2014 talks page). Sec. I naive interpretation and its failure; ergodicity argument against Page-Wootters ('manifestly not viable for sufficiently complicated (i.e., ergodic) systems'); conditional probability interpretation Eqs. (1.14)-(1.15) and the measure/conditioning-variable problems; 'Heraclitian property' definition; parametrized particle model Eqs. (1.16)-(1.37); 'no perfect clock' theorem with proof between Eqs. (1.38)-(1.39) and footnote 16 noting the conflict with Peres 1980; observer-incorporation discussion; Sec. III proposal corresponding to GR with unspecified cosmological constant
assumptions: Canonical (minisuperspace) quantum gravity with Hamiltonian constraint; for the theorem: ordinary Schrodinger QM with Hamiltonian bounded from below; measurements at instants; single-observer interpretation
conclusion: Authors' claims: the conditional probability interpretation requires a preferred time variable (or class) not specified by the theory, and a probability measure on the conditioning variable that carries as much information as the wave function itself; no dynamical variable of a system with lower-bounded Hamiltonian can correlate monotonically with Schrodinger time (theorem); Page-Wootters stationary-observable dynamics is not viable for ergodic systems; incorporating observers as ordinary dynamical systems does not alleviate the interpretive problems; they propose instead a theory with an explicit nondynamical time parameter (classically GR with arbitrary unspecified cosmological constant, viable in minisuperspace but possibly observable-poor in general)
proof_status: Primary PDF read end to end; the no-perfect-clock proof (holomorphy of f(t)=<T_n|e^{-iHt}|T_m> in the lower half t-plane) read in detail, not independently reproduced
dependencies: Dirac quantization; WKB interpretation; Peres 1980 AJP clock construction (conflicting claim noted by the authors themselves, footnote 16)
open_questions: How the no-perfect-clock theorem interacts with covariant-POVM (non-orthogonal time states) clocks: the theorem constrains monotonic ideal clocks, while POVM clocks are approximate by design; whether bounded-clock proposals (Maccone-Sacha) evade or just accept non-monotonicity is contested in pw-cavendish-unphysical-2024 vs pw-maccone-reply-2025
relevance: Strongest classical published critique of relational/conditional time: names the preferred-variable problem, the measure ambiguity, and proves a spectral no-go used by later critics
limits: 1989 setting (minisuperspace, noninteracting clock and system); the theorem concerns monotonic 'perfect' clocks and does not directly address modern covariant-POVM or periodic-clock constructions; their alternative proposal is not established as empirically viable for general spacetimes (authors' own caveat)

title: Group averaging, positive definiteness and superselection sectors

(8)-(12): effective Hamiltonian H_eff^A=[I+f(X_M)]^{-1} H_M non-Hermitian since the factor does not commute with H_M; Sec. 'Gravitationally interacting clocks' Eqs. (13)-(15): both clock perspectives non-Hermitian when relative positions change; Sec. 'Parametrization by time states' Eqs. title: The time of arrival problem in the Page-Wootters formalism
version: arXiv:2604.00092v1 (submitted 2026-03-31; only version)
locators: Sec. II PW formalism with covariant POVM clock, physical inner product <psi|delta(C)|phi> and reduction maps R_C(t) (Eqs. 1-13); Sec. II.3 free-particle case: constraint factorization C=C_+ C_-, direct-sum decomposition of physical Hilbert space (Eqs. 14-19) and superselection between +/- momentum sectors, requirement R_- ⊆ spec(H_C) for a free-particle relational picture; Sec. III inverted conditioning via sector-adapted states |x_0,sigma> (Eqs. 23-27) and relational ToA distribution Eq. (29-30) coinciding with Kijowski's; Sec. IV conditional-probability analysis: two-clock example Eq. (31) where Pr[t_a|t_b]=Pr[t_b|t_a] both equal the would-be joint and the naive denominator equals 1 for all t_a; Sec. V discussion: periodic-clock proposal (Maccone-Sacha) physically distinct; prediction of no interference between counter-propagating wavepackets as an empirical falsifier; Appendix A general sector-wise reduction for quadratic Hamiltonians
assumptions: Free-particle system; clock Hamiltonian with continuous spectrum including R_-; no clock-system interaction; conditioning via POVM covariant with respect to H_C
conclusion: Authors' claims: the PW 'conditional probabilities' are not ordinary conditional probabilities derived from joint and marginal distributions, because physical states do not factorize and kinematical expressions diverge for continuous-spectrum constraints; reduction maps are only partial isometries per superselection sector; the naive position-conditioning is non-invertible and non-normalizable; their sector-adapted relational ToA distribution equals Kijowski's, with the momentum-branch separation derived rather than assumed; the framework predicts non-interference between counter-propagating wavepackets in arrival times
proof_status: Full text (HTML, all sections and appendix listing) read; the Kijowski-coincidence read at equation level, not independently reproduced
dependencies: Höhn-Smith-Lock trinity (their Sec. VI is cited for the critical discussion of 'time from entanglement'); Smith-Ahmadi; Höhn et al. periodic clocks NJP 28, 034504 (2026); Maccone-Sacha and its critique/reply; Kijowski 1974
open_questions: Authors': extension to interactions and external potentials; whether another relational choice within PW could yield a different ToA distribution (they show any choice respecting their three conditions keeps sector separation); whether the non-interference prediction is observed experimentally
relevance: The most precise recent technical critique of the conditional-probability reading of PW, plus a falsifiable prediction
limits: Preprint, single version; free-particle, noninteracting case; no detector dynamics (inherited from Kijowski, as the authors note)

title: The clock ambiguity problem: extended or extinguished?
assumptions: Purely relational stance; no fixed clock-world split; ideal clock spectra
conclusion: Authors' claims: the clock ambiguity (attributed to Albrecht 1995 in their abstract, with the Albrecht-Iglesias 2008 paper as its published form) cannot be solved by purely relational conditions like noninteraction; it extends from histories to the evolution laws themselves - the spectrum of any ideal clock uniformizes the spectra of the world's evolution operators, leaving only Hilbert-space dimension as invariant; the ambiguity is resolved by specifying the physical meaning of observables
open_questions: What exactly counts as 'physical meaning of observables' without importing time (the paper's stated solution needs scrutiny at full text)
relevance: Strongest recent sharpening of the clock-ambiguity objection
limits: Abstract-level; preprint

title: Watching the Clocks: Interpreting the Page-Wootters Formalism and the Internal Quantum Reference Frame Programme
version: Foundations of Physics 52, 99 (2022); DOI 10.1007/s10701-022-00620-7 (Crossref verified); arXiv:2203.06755v1 (2022-03-13) abstract read via arXiv; the Chapman digitalcommons postprint PDF and ResearchGate/academia copies were bot-blocked this session, so section-level claims are not quoted
assumptions: PW and IQRF formalisms; single-world realist reading sought via a 'final measurement' approach
conclusion: Author's abstract claims: there are difficulties interpreting PW/IQRF; the invoked 'reference frames' may not be operationally meaningful without a prior interpretation, hence unsuitable for defining an equivalence principle; the notion of superposition should account for embedding of instantaneous states in dynamical evolution, complicating 'relativity of superposition'; typically the operational content appears only in the limit where at least one reference system becomes large, so the formalisms' role is to show how macroscopic reference frames emerge from relational facts
dependencies: Page-Wootters; internal QRF programme (Hohn et al.)
open_questions: Her specific argument sections (self-reference, measurement) need the full text before being cited in detail; Vanrietvelde 2026 (frontier lane) explicitly defers her criticism as unaddressed
relevance: The main current philosophical critique of PW and temporal QRFs; recorded as unanswered by the QRF lane's own 2026 operational-meaning paper
limits: Abstract-only this session despite multiple access attempts (Chapman Cloudflare, arXiv HTML not fetched for sections)
